reason: The cited evidence does not address the WTaTiVZr alloy or its constituent elements. E1 describes dislocation-solute interactions in a different W-based HEA with a lamellar structure, not short-range ordering or grain boundary sliding. E2 reports grain boundary sliding and dynamic recrystallization in TaNbHfZrTi, an alloy with a different composition and crystal structure, and does not link these to solute-induced short-range ordering. The key premises about solute-induced ordering, slip system activation, and dynamic recovery in WTaTiVZr are unsupported by the cited passages.
premises: Refractory solutes in WTaTiVZr cause local lattice distortions and short-range chemical ordering
Short-range ordering activates additional dislocation slip systems
Short-range ordering promotes dynamic recovery mechanisms such as grain boundary sliding
These mechanisms delay crack initiation and increase plastic strain and toughness relative to pure tungsten
The proposed mechanisms operate at 1000–1500 °C under plasma-facing-component conditions
